```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Source and models

```{r models, include = FALSE}
mod_orr <- readModelDb("Sangro_2023_nivolumab_ipilimumab_orr")
mod_os <- readModelDb("Sangro_2023_nivolumab_ipilimumab_os")
mod_nivo <- readModelDb("Bajaj_2017_nivolumab")
mod_ipi <- readModelDb("Sanghavi_2020_ipilimumab")
meta_orr <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_orr)$meta
```

* Citation: `r meta_orr$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13544>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10432868/>
* Supporting Information (Data S1; Tables S1-S3 and Figures S1-S3):
  distributed with the open-access article.

Sangro 2023 is an exposure-response analysis of CheckMate 040 in
sorafenib-experienced patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
It fits two separate efficacy models, and this package carries each as its own
file:

| Model file | Endpoint | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Sangro_2023_nivolumab_ipilimumab_orr` | Objective tumor response (OTR) by blinded independent central review, logistic regression | Table 2 |
| `Sangro_2023_nivolumab_ipilimumab_os` | Overall survival, Cox proportional hazards (relative hazard only) | Table 3 |

Both models are driven by the model-predicted average serum concentration over
the **first** dosing interval (Cavg1) of nivolumab (`CAV_NIVOLUMAB`) and of
ipilimumab (`CAV_IPILIMUMAB`). The authors derived Cavg1 from updated versions
of two population PK models that this package also carries,
`Bajaj_2017_nivolumab` and `Sanghavi_2020_ipilimumab`. Those updated refits are
not reported, so this vignette regenerates Cavg1 from the published originals
and compares the result with Table S2.

The safety analysis (hepatic treatment-related and immune-mediated adverse
events, Table 4) is descriptive incidence by arm with no fitted model, so there
is nothing to encode from it.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_os)$meta$population
```

The analysis population is `r pop$n_subjects` sorafenib-experienced adults from
CheckMate 040 (Sangro 2023 Table 1): 182 received nivolumab monotherapy
0.1-10 mg/kg every 2 weeks (cohorts 1 and 2) and 146 received nivolumab plus
ipilimumab in cohort 4:

* **Arm A**: nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four
  doses, then nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (n = 49).
* **Arm B**: nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four
  doses, then nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (n = 49).
* **Arm C**: nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks
  (n = 48).

Median age was 62 years (18-83), median weight 67 kg (38-130), and
`r pop$sex_female_pct`% were female. 46% were Asian and 41% White. ECOG
performance status was 0 in 60% and 1 in 40%. Child-Pugh class was A in 98%,
and 86% had extrahepatic spread or vascular invasion. HCC etiology was hepatitis
B in 41%, hepatitis C in 20% and uninfected in 37%.

# Coefficient check against the printed odds and hazard ratios

Every coefficient is printed together with its odds or hazard ratio, so
`exp(coefficient)` must reproduce the printed ratio to its printed precision.

```{r coef-check}
ini_orr <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_orr)$iniDf
ini_os <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_os)$iniDf
coef_of <- function(ini, nm) ini$est[ini$name == nm]

coef_tbl <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model, ~parameter, ~printed_ratio,
  "OTR", "logit_ref", 0.242,
  "OTR", "e_cav_nivolumab_logit", 0.9916,
  "OTR", "e_cav_ipilimumab_logit", 1.45,
  "OS", "e_cav_nivolumab_haz", 1.081,
  "OS", "e_cav_ipilimumab_haz", 0.8574,
  "OS", "e_ecog_ge1_haz", 1.56,
  "OS", "e_cli_haz", 1.052,
  "OS", "e_ldhr_haz", 2.217
) |>
  mutate(
    estimate = mapply(
      function(m, p) coef_of(if (m == "OTR") ini_orr else ini_os, p),
      model,
      parameter
    ),
    exp_estimate = exp(estimate),
    pct_diff = 100 * (exp_estimate - printed_ratio) / printed_ratio
  )

coef_tbl |>
  mutate(across(c(exp_estimate, pct_diff), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Model = model,
    Parameter = parameter,
    Estimate = estimate,
    "exp(estimate)" = exp_estimate,
    "Printed ratio" = printed_ratio,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "exp(coefficient) against the odds / hazard ratios printed in Sangro 2023 Tables 2 and 3.")

# The ratios are printed to three or four significant figures.
stopifnot(all(abs(coef_tbl$pct_diff) < 0.5))
```

# Arm-level odds and hazard ratios against Figures 2 and 3

Figures 2 and 3 plot, for each treatment, the odds or hazard ratio relative to a
nivolumab-monotherapy reference (nivolumab Cavg1 25 ug/mL, no ipilimumab), as a
bar spanning the 5th to 95th percentiles of the arm's exposures. The ratio at the
arm's **geometric-mean** exposures must fall inside that bar. Only the two
exposure terms enter these ratios; every other covariate is held equal and
cancels.

```{r arm-ratios}
logit_or <- function(cav_n, cav_i) {
  li <- ifelse(cav_i > 0, log(cav_i), 0)
  coef_of(ini_orr, "e_cav_nivolumab_logit") *
    cav_n +
    coef_of(ini_orr, "e_cav_ipilimumab_logit") * li
}
log_hr <- function(cav_n, cav_i) {
  li <- ifelse(cav_i > 0, log(cav_i), 0)
  coef_of(ini_os, "e_cav_nivolumab_haz") *
    log(cav_n) +
    coef_of(ini_os, "e_cav_ipilimumab_haz") * li
}
cav_ref <- 25

arm_gm <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~cav_n, ~cav_i_s2, ~cav_i_text, ~or_p05, ~or_p95, ~hr_p05, ~hr_p95,
  "Arm A", 6.5, 17.5, 16.7, 2.92, 3.70, 0.56, 0.60,
  "Arm B", 21.5, 5.8, 5.1, 1.05, 2.10, 0.73, 0.98,
  "Arm C", 23.0, 2.3, 1.7, 0.83, 1.70, 0.79, 1.08,
  "NIVO3 q2w", 24.8, 0, 0, 0.95, 1.10, 0.97, 1.02
) |>
  mutate(
    or_s2 = exp(logit_or(cav_n, cav_i_s2) - logit_or(cav_ref, 0)),
    or_text = exp(logit_or(cav_n, cav_i_text) - logit_or(cav_ref, 0)),
    hr_s2 = exp(log_hr(cav_n, cav_i_s2) - log_hr(cav_ref, 0)),
    hr_text = exp(log_hr(cav_n, cav_i_text) - log_hr(cav_ref, 0))
  )

arm_gm |>
  transmute(
    Treatment = arm,
    "OR at Table S2 GM" = round(or_s2, 2),
    "OR at Results-text GM" = round(or_text, 2),
    "Figure 2 P05-P95" = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", or_p05, or_p95),
    "HR at Table S2 GM" = round(hr_s2, 3),
    "HR at Results-text GM" = round(hr_text, 3),
    "Figure 3 P05-P95" = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", hr_p05, hr_p95)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Odds ratio (objective response) and hazard ratio (death) at each arm's geometric-mean Cavg1, relative to nivolumab Cavg1 25 ug/mL without ipilimumab, against the percentile bars of Sangro 2023 Figures 2 and 3.")

stopifnot(
  all(arm_gm$or_s2 >= arm_gm$or_p05 & arm_gm$or_s2 <= arm_gm$or_p95),
  all(arm_gm$hr_s2 >= arm_gm$hr_p05 & arm_gm$hr_s2 <= arm_gm$hr_p95)
)
```

Both geometric-mean sets land inside every bar. This check also settles two
choices the paper does not print:

* **Natural logarithm.** With log10 the arm A odds ratio would be
  `r round(exp(0.3712 * log10(17.5) - 0.00841 * (6.5 - 25)), 2)`, well below
  the plotted 2.92-3.70; the natural log gives
  `r round(arm_gm$or_s2[1], 2)`.
* **log(Cavg1), with the term set to 0 when there is no ipilimumab.** Arm C's
  5th-percentile odds ratio (0.83) and hazard ratio (0.79) sit on the far side
  of 1 from the ipilimumab effect, which needs a negative ipilimumab term for
  patients with Cavg1 below 1 ug/mL. log(Cavg1 + 1) can never be negative, and
  the arm's nivolumab exposures (geometric mean 23.0 against the reference 25)
  are too close to the reference to produce those bars on their own.

# Predicted against observed objective response

At each group's Table S2 geometric-mean exposures, the fitted response
probability is compared with the observed OTR and its 95% CI from the same
table. This is a coarse check: the mean of individual probabilities differs from
the probability at the geometric-mean exposure, and the groups are small.

```{r orr-observed}
# The logistic model has no between-subject variability, so rxode2 warns
# that a multi-subject solve has no omega. That is expected here; only that
# one warning is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}

solve_orr <- function(cav_n, cav_i) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = seq_along(cav_n),
    time = 0,
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    CAV_NIVOLUMAB = cav_n,
    CAV_IPILIMUMAB = cav_i
  )
  muffle_no_omega(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_orr,
    events = ev,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )))$prob_orr_central
}

orr_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~n, ~cav_n, ~cav_i, ~otr, ~otr_lo, ~otr_hi,
  "NIVO<3 q2w", 18, 3.8, 0, 0.22, 0.06, 0.48,
  "NIVO3 q2w", 154, 24.8, 0, 0.14, 0.09, 0.21,
  "NIVO10 q2w", 10, 86.8, 0, 0.00, 0.00, 0.31,
  "Arm A", 49, 6.5, 17.5, 0.33, 0.20, 0.48,
  "Arm B", 49, 21.5, 5.8, 0.31, 0.18, 0.45,
  "Arm C", 48, 23.0, 2.3, 0.31, 0.19, 0.46
) |>
  mutate(pred = solve_orr(cav_n, cav_i))

orr_obs |>
  transmute(
    Group = group,
    N = n,
    "Nivolumab Cavg1 (ug/mL)" = cav_n,
    "Ipilimumab Cavg1 (ug/mL)" = cav_i,
    "Predicted Pr(OTR)" = round(pred, 3),
    "Observed OTR (95% CI)" = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", otr, otr_lo, otr_hi)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Predicted probability of objective response at each group's geometric-mean Cavg1 against the observed OTR of Sangro 2023 Table S2.")

stopifnot(all(orr_obs$pred >= orr_obs$otr_lo & orr_obs$pred <= orr_obs$otr_hi))
```

Every prediction falls inside the observed 95% CI. Arm C is under-predicted
(0.21 against 0.31), consistent with the authors' remark that first-dose
ipilimumab exposure under-represents continuous every-6-weeks dosing.

# Regenerating Cavg1 from the upstream PK models

## Virtual cohort

One hundred virtual patients per treatment are drawn from the Table 1
demographics. Nivolumab is simulated with `Bajaj_2017_nivolumab` and
ipilimumab with `Sanghavi_2020_ipilimumab`. The Sanghavi covariates are set for
second-line HCC (`LINE_1L = 0`, `TUMTP_SCLC = 0`), combination therapy
(`COMBO_NIVO = 1`) and each arm's nivolumab regimen (`NIVO_1Q3W = 1` in arm A,
`NIVO_3Q2W = 1` in arm C; arm B's 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks was not retained as a
covariate in Sanghavi 2020).

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230510)
n_per_arm <- 100

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm, ~nivo_mgkg, ~nivo_tau, ~ipi_mgkg, ~ipi_tau,
  "NIVO3 q2w", 3, 14, 0, NA,
  "NIVO10 q2w", 10, 14, 0, NA,
  "Arm A", 1, 21, 3, 21,
  "Arm B", 3, 21, 1, 21,
  "Arm C", 3, 14, 1, 42
)

cohort <- arms[rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), each = n_per_arm), ] |>
  mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), log(67), 0.2)), 38), 130),
    SEXF = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.21),
    RACE_ASIAN = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.46),
    ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(dplyr::n(), 1, 0.40),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 85, 20), 30), 150),
    LDH = exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), log(220), 0.35)),
    TUMTP_SCLC = 0,
    LINE_1L = 0,
    COMBO_NIVO = 1,
    NIVO_1Q3W = as.integer(arm == "Arm A"),
    NIVO_3Q2W = as.integer(arm == "Arm C")
  )
```

## First-dose simulation

Only the first dose matters for Cavg1, so a single dose is simulated and
observed through the end of the first dosing interval.

```{r simulate-pk}
obs_grid <- c(0, 1 / 24, 2 / 24, 0.25, 0.5, 1:42)

first_dose_events <- function(cohort, mgkg, tau, dur) {
  dose <- cohort |>
    transmute(
      id,
      time = 0,
      amt = .data[[mgkg]] * WT,
      evid = 1L,
      cmt = "central",
      dur = dur
    )
  obs <- cohort |>
    select(id, tau = all_of(tau)) |>
    rowwise() |>
    reframe(id, time = obs_grid[obs_grid <= tau]) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dur = 0)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_nivo <- first_dose_events(cohort, "nivo_mgkg", "nivo_tau", dur = 1 / 24)
sim_nivo <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_nivo,
  events = ev_nivo,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "arm"
))

cohort_ipi <- cohort |> dplyr::filter(ipi_mgkg > 0)
ev_ipi <- first_dose_events(cohort_ipi, "ipi_mgkg", "ipi_tau", dur = 1.5 / 24)
sim_ipi <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_ipi,
  events = ev_ipi,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "arm"
))
```

## Cavg1 by PKNCA

Cavg1 is the PKNCA average concentration over the first dosing interval
(`cav` from 0 to tau), with tau set per drug and arm.

```{r pknca}
run_cav <- function(sim, cohort, mgkg, tau) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, arm, time, Cc)
  doses <- cohort |>
    transmute(id, arm, time = 0, dose = .data[[mgkg]] * WT)
  intervals <- cohort |>
    distinct(arm, end = .data[[tau]]) |>
    mutate(start = 0, cav = TRUE)
  o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
  o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, dose ~ time | arm + id)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
    select(id, arm, cav = PPORRES)
}

cav_nivo <- run_cav(sim_nivo, cohort, "nivo_mgkg", "nivo_tau")
cav_ipi <- run_cav(sim_ipi, cohort_ipi, "ipi_mgkg", "ipi_tau")
```

```{r cav-compare}
gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
sim_gm <- bind_rows(
  cav_nivo |> mutate(drug = "Nivolumab"),
  cav_ipi |> mutate(drug = "Ipilimumab")
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, "-", arm)) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(cav = gm(cav), .groups = "drop")

ref_gm <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cav,
  "Nivolumab - NIVO3 q2w", 24.8,
  "Nivolumab - NIVO10 q2w", 86.8,
  "Nivolumab - Arm A", 6.5,
  "Nivolumab - Arm B", 21.5,
  "Nivolumab - Arm C", 23.0,
  "Ipilimumab - Arm A", 17.5,
  "Ipilimumab - Arm B", 5.8,
  "Ipilimumab - Arm C", 2.3
)

cav_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_gm,
  reference = ref_gm,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cav = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cav_cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Geometric-mean first-dose Cavg1 regenerated from the published Bajaj 2017",
    "and Sanghavi 2020 models against Sangro 2023 Table S2 (which used",
    "updated refits). * differs by more than 20%."
  )
)

chk_cav <- left_join(sim_gm, ref_gm, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (cav_sim - cav_ref) / cav_ref)
stopifnot(
  # Every nivolumab group and ipilimumab arms A and B reproduce Table S2.
  all(abs(chk_cav$pct[chk_cav$treatment != "Ipilimumab - Arm C"]) < 20),
  # Arm C ipilimumab is the known outlier (see Assumptions); its ordering holds.
  with(
    chk_cav,
    cav_sim[treatment == "Ipilimumab - Arm A"] >
      cav_sim[treatment == "Ipilimumab - Arm B"] &
      cav_sim[treatment == "Ipilimumab - Arm B"] >
        cav_sim[treatment == "Ipilimumab - Arm C"]
  )
)
```

```{r fig1, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1 of Sangro 2023: distribution of first-dose Cavg1 by treatment, regenerated from the published population PK models. Diamonds are the Table S2 geometric means."}
cav_long <- bind_rows(
  cav_nivo |> mutate(drug = "Nivolumab Cavg1"),
  cav_ipi |> mutate(drug = "Ipilimumab Cavg1")
) |>
  mutate(drug = factor(drug, levels = c("Nivolumab Cavg1", "Ipilimumab Cavg1")))
ref_long <- ref_gm |>
  tidyr::separate(treatment, c("drug", "arm"), sep = " - ") |>
  mutate(
    drug = factor(paste(drug, "Cavg1"), levels = c("Nivolumab Cavg1", "Ipilimumab Cavg1"))
  )
ggplot(cav_long, aes(arm, cav)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = ref_long, colour = "firebrick", shape = 18, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cavg1 (ug/mL)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

# Odds and hazard ratios across the regenerated cohort

The regenerated per-patient exposures are passed through both models. As in
Figures 2 and 3, each ratio is taken against nivolumab Cavg1 25 ug/mL without
ipilimumab, with all other covariates equal (so only the two exposure terms
contribute). The OS model is solved with `ECOG_GE1 = 0`, `LDHR = 1` and the
Bajaj 2017 reference clearance for every patient, and the same reference
patient is solved at the reference exposure.

```{r cohort-ratios}
er <- cav_nivo |>
  rename(CAV_NIVOLUMAB = cav) |>
  left_join(cav_ipi |> rename(CAV_IPILIMUMAB = cav), by = c("id", "arm")) |>
  mutate(CAV_IPILIMUMAB = dplyr::coalesce(CAV_IPILIMUMAB, 0))

ref_row <- tibble::tibble(id = 0L, arm = "reference", CAV_NIVOLUMAB = cav_ref, CAV_IPILIMUMAB = 0)
er_in <- bind_rows(ref_row, er) |>
  mutate(
    time = 0,
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    ECOG_GE1 = 0,
    LDHR = 1,
    CLI = 9.4 / 1000,
    sid = dplyr::row_number()
  )
ev_er <- er_in |> select(id = sid, time, amt, evid, CAV_NIVOLUMAB, CAV_IPILIMUMAB, ECOG_GE1, LDHR, CLI)

p_orr <- muffle_no_omega(as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_orr, events = ev_er, returnType = "data.frame")))
p_os <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_os, events = ev_er, returnType = "data.frame"))

er_in <- er_in |>
  mutate(
    logit = qlogis(p_orr$prob_orr_central),
    or = exp(logit - logit[1]),
    hr = p_os$hr / p_os$hr[1]
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(arm != "reference")

fig_bars <- arm_gm |>
  select(arm, or_p05, or_p95, hr_p05, hr_p95)
cohort_ratio <- er_in |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    or_med = median(or),
    or_q05 = quantile(or, 0.05),
    or_q95 = quantile(or, 0.95),
    hr_med = median(hr),
    hr_q05 = quantile(hr, 0.05),
    hr_q95 = quantile(hr, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(fig_bars, by = "arm")

cohort_ratio |>
  transmute(
    Treatment = arm,
    "OR median (P05-P95)" = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", or_med, or_q05, or_q95),
    "Figure 2 P05-P95" = ifelse(is.na(or_p05), "--", sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", or_p05, or_p95)),
    "HR median (P05-P95)" = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", hr_med, hr_q05, hr_q95),
    "Figure 3 P05-P95" = ifelse(is.na(hr_p05), "--", sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", hr_p05, hr_p95))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Odds and hazard ratios across the regenerated cohort against the percentile bars of Sangro 2023 Figures 2 and 3.")

# For arms A and B, whose regenerated exposures match Table S2, the cohort
# median ratio must agree with the ratio at the Table S2 geometric means
# (checked against Figures 2 and 3 above). The comparison is on the median,
# not on the published bar edges: arm B's median sits next to the top of its
# Figure 2 bar, and which side of the edge it lands on depends on the random
# draw. Arm C is excluded for the reason given above.
ab <- dplyr::filter(cohort_ratio, arm %in% c("Arm A", "Arm B")) |>
  left_join(select(arm_gm, arm, or_s2, hr_s2), by = "arm")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ab$or_med / ab$or_s2 - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(ab$hr_med / ab$hr_s2 - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

```{r fig23, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figures 2 and 3 of Sangro 2023: per-patient odds ratio of objective response and hazard ratio of death relative to nivolumab Cavg1 25 ug/mL without ipilimumab. Boxes: regenerated cohort; red bars: published P05-P95."}
plot_df <- er_in |>
  select(arm, or, hr) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(or, hr), names_to = "ratio", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(ratio = ifelse(ratio == "or", "Odds ratio, OTR (Figure 2)", "Hazard ratio, OS (Figure 3)"))
bar_df <- bind_rows(
  fig_bars |> transmute(arm, lo = or_p05, hi = or_p95, ratio = "Odds ratio, OTR (Figure 2)"),
  fig_bars |> transmute(arm, lo = hr_p05, hi = hr_p95, ratio = "Hazard ratio, OS (Figure 3)")
)
ggplot(plot_df, aes(arm, value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = bar_df,
    aes(x = arm, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "firebrick",
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ratio, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ratio relative to reference") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Zero ipilimumab exposure.** Both models take the natural log of ipilimumab
  Cavg1, which is 0 for every monotherapy patient. The log term is set to 0 when
  `CAV_IPILIMUMAB = 0`. The paper does not print this choice; it is the only
  handling that reproduces the arm-level bars of Figures 2 and 3 (see above).
* **Natural logarithm.** "Log-transformed" is read as the natural log for both
  Cavg1 terms and for LDH/ULN. The Cavg1 base is fixed by Figure 2 (log10 would
  put arm A's odds ratio at 1.85, outside 2.92-3.70). The LDH/ULN base cannot be
  checked against any printed quantity, and the same natural log is assumed.
* **Baseline nivolumab clearance units.** Table 3 gives the coefficient per
  mL/h. The model takes `CLI` in the canonical L/h and multiplies by 1000.
* **No baseline hazard.** A Cox model leaves h0(t) unspecified, so the OS model
  returns the relative hazard `hr` only. The predicted Kaplan-Meier curves of
  Figure S1 cannot be reproduced from the published information.
* **Placeholder residual.** The logistic model is deterministic; the fixed
  additive SD of 0.001 on `prob_orr_central` exists only because rxode2
  requires an observation declaration.
* **Upstream PK.** Sangro 2023 used updated refits of the Bajaj 2017 and
  Sanghavi 2020 models that are not published. This vignette uses the
  published originals, with assumed infusion durations of 1 hour (nivolumab)
  and 1.5 hours (ipilimumab), and Table 1-based demographics (log-normal weight
  around 67 kg, eGFR around 85 mL/min/1.73 m^2 and LDH around 220 U/L, which
  Table 1 does not report). The regenerated geometric means match Table S2
  within 20% for every nivolumab group and for ipilimumab in arms A and B.
* **Arm C ipilimumab Cavg1.** The regenerated arm C ipilimumab geometric mean is
  about 70% above Table S2's 2.3 ug/mL (the Results text gives 1.7). For a
  single 1 mg/kg dose, the 0-42-day average cannot fall below half the
  0-21-day average of arm B unless clearance is materially higher, yet Table S2 gives
  2.3 / 5.8 = 0.40 and the text 1.7 / 5.1 = 0.33. The paper does not say how
  the 6-weekly averaging window was defined, so the discrepancy is reported
  rather than resolved, and arm C is excluded from the regenerated-cohort gate.
* **Two sets of ipilimumab geometric means.** The Results text (16.7 / 5.1 /
  1.7 ug/mL) and Table S2 (17.5 / 5.8 / 2.3 ug/mL) differ slightly; both are
  shown above and both satisfy the Figure 2 and 3 checks. Table S2 is used
  elsewhere because it also gives the nivolumab values.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** OTR: etiology, PD-L1 status, ECOG,
  tumor size, extrahepatic spread or vascular invasion, and baseline nivolumab
  clearance. OS: etiology, alpha-fetoprotein, tumor size and albumin. No
  estimates are reported for them; they are listed in each model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction to Sangro 2023 was found (checked
  2026-11-06).
